blocks.text: Premier Energies makes crystalline-silicon solar cells and solar modules in Telangana and sells them almost entirely inside India [F] (AR2026 p.275). In FY26 it had 3.6 GW of installed cell capacity and 11.1 GW of module capacity; it produced 2,268 MW of cells and 3,570 MW of modules [F] (AR2026 p.15). It makes money in two ways: it sells cells to other Indian module makers, and it sells modules to developers, EPC contractors, commercial and industrial (C&I) buyers and retail channel partners. The most valuable modules are 'DCR' modules. These are built with domestically made cells and qualify under India's domestic-content rules (ALMM-II), and they sell for much more than modules built with imported cells [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Management quotes about Rs 2.2-2.3 crore per MW for DCR modules against Rs 1.4-1.5 crore per MW for non-DCR modules [MC] (CALL Jan 2026).

It gives no percentage split by end market, and we treat that as a disclosure gap [AI].

This means only about two years of public quarterly disclosure exist. The prospectus was not among the documents we had, so pre-IPO customer, order and related-party history cannot be checked here [AI].

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. The price is above every scenario in our DCR model. At Rs 870 the stock trades above the bull-case fair value of Rs 729.6. The reverse DCF implies 36.6% annual sales growth for five years, against 19.8% in the base case [E] (NUMBERS).

2. The margin is created by policy. Management says non-DCR business 'is not profitable as we speak' because India has about 250 GW of module lines against about 60 GW of demand [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Any softening of ALMM or duty protection would expose that gap. The C&I and residential ALMM-II exemption to December 2026 shows the rules can move [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

3. A step-up in depreciation is coming. Quarterly depreciation was Rs 96 crore in Q1 FY27 [F] (NUMBERS), and management guides to about Rs 240-250 crore per quarter in Q3-Q4 FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). That is roughly Rs 110-117 crore of post-tax profit per quarter, about a quarter of Q1 PAT, assuming a 24% tax rate [E].

4. Growth is funded with debt and could bring dilution. FCF was -Rs 1,736 crore in FY26, borrowings rose from Rs 1,954 crore to Rs 3,707 crore [F] (NUMBERS), and the September 2026 AGM proposed a Rs 5,000 crore capital-raise enabling resolution [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

5. Execution timelines have slipped repeatedly. The 4.8 GW cell block was due in June 2026 [MC] (CALL Jan 2026) but trial runs of the 7 GW line were only expected in late August [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). BESS phase 1 moved from June 2026 [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) to June 2027 [F] (AR2026 p.31). The KSolare acquisition, described as 'completed' in November 2025, was abandoned [F] (AR2026 p.291).

6. FY26 EBITDA was helped by non-recurring or judgement-driven items. The liquidated-damages line in revenue swung from -Rs 79.6 crore to +Rs 76.9 crore [F] (AR2026 p.263), and the warranty charge fell from Rs 136 crore to Rs 61 crore while module revenue rose 33% [F] (AR2026 p.265).
7. Cash conversion weakened. CFO/PAT was 0.84 in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS), inventory rose Rs 711 crore, and finished goods almost doubled to Rs 643 crore [F] (AR2026 p.264).

8. The promoter is selling. Promoter holding fell from 63.94% to 58.48% in the June 2026 quarter [F] (NUMBERS), while the MD personally guarantees Rs 3,773 crore of group borrowings [F] (AR2026 p.257).

9. Technology risk is built into the asset base. Five-year useful lives and Rs 182 crore of accelerated depreciation in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.265) show how quickly lines become obsolete. Management places the TOPCon efficiency ceiling at about 26% [MC] (CALL May 2026).
10. The company is almost entirely exposed to one country. It is 99% domestic, and the US imposed a preliminary 125.87% countervailing duty on Indian cells in February 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.25).

Is the 30% margin structural or a policy rent? Bulls cite five quarters at 29-31% [F] (NUMBERS). Bears note that management itself says module-level margins 'have almost completely vanished' and that the profit pool now sits in cells [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). If cell capacity catches up with demand, that pool shrinks [AI].

Is the order book as firm as described? Management says orders are 'signed, confirmed with advances received' [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). The Rs 940 crore of customer advances is about 6.7% of the March 2026 book [E] (AR2026 p.262). Pricing is variable for wafer, silver and FX [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The book protects volume more than it protects margin [AI].

Is the market underestimating the depreciation and interest step-up? TTM PAT of Rs 1,674 crore [F] (NUMBERS) includes only Rs 96 crore of Q1 depreciation. The 7 GW line and Seetharampur add Rs 150 crore or more per quarter [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

Could the market be too pessimistic about new businesses? Transcon's Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA margin of 24.3% [F] (PPT Aug 2026) and a 10 GVA EHV plant [MC] (PPT Aug 2026) could matter more than the current Rs 110 crore quarterly revenue suggests [AI].

blocks.text: Our view differs from the consensus framing in one respect [AI]. The consensus sees an integrated leader whose margins are protected by scale and technology. We see the FY26-Q1 FY27 margins as the peak of a policy-created shortage of DCR cells. Reported earnings benefited from a lower depreciation run-rate, a positive liquidated-damages swing and a lighter warranty charge, and all three are temporary or discretionary [AI]. The company is executing well; cell utilisation was 92% in Q1 FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). But the share price already discounts more than the bull case in our DCF model [E] (NUMBERS). Even flawless delivery of the 7 GW line and the transformer ramp would leave the valuation needing either an extension of policy protection or a successful move up the value chain into wafers [AI].

Subsidiary revenues add up to far more than the consolidated Rs 7,824 crore, which shows heavy intra-group cell and module flows [E] (AR2026 p.48-49). Associates are Mavyatho Ventures (30%) and Brightstone Developers (28.01% direct and indirect) [F] (AR2026 p.51). Five subsidiaries had not started operations at March 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.50).

The company is 31 years old, but the current business is only about three years old [AI]. Revenue was Rs 743 crore in FY22 and the company made losses in FY22 and FY23 [F] (NUMBERS). The TOPCon cell line dates from July 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.28), and the 5.6 GW module plant from March 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.28). About 90% of today's cell capacity will be less than a year old by March 2027 if the 7 GW line starts on schedule [E]. The through-cycle record of this asset base is therefore very short. The high-margin years, FY25 and FY26, coincide with the start of ALMM protection and DCR demand [AI].

items: 1. Polysilicon, ingots and wafers are bought in. There is no in-house ingot or wafer capacity today; a 10 GW facility is under construction [F] (AR2026 p.6). Wafer pricing is passed through in long-term cell contracts [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

2. Cells: wafers are converted into Mono PERC (M10R) and TOPCon (G12R 16BB and 0BB) cells with stated mass-production efficiency of up to 25.5% [MC] (AR2026 p.30). Silver paste is the key consumable [MC] (CALL Jan 2026).

3. Modules: cells are stringed and laminated with glass, EVA, backsheet or second glass and an aluminium frame into modules of up to 630 Wp [MC] (AR2026 p.30). Aluminium is about 11% of module cost [MC] (CALL May 2026).
4. Channel: large IPP, EPC and C&I orders are booked direct. Rooftop and PM Surya Ghar volumes go through cash-and-carry distributors and OEM brands [MC] (CALL May 2026, CALL Jan 2026).
5. Downstream and adjacent: small EPC/O&M business (Rs 162 crore in FY26) [F] (AR2026 p.262); transformers (Transcon); planned BESS assembly and aluminium frames [F] (AR2026 p.6).

blocks.text: Management says the profit pool has moved upstream: 'Margins have almost completely vanished at the module manufacturing end, and the entire profitability pool has shifted upstream to the cell business' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). They expect ALMM-III to push it further upstream into ingot and wafer [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). On this basis, Premier's value capture today sits in turning domestically made cells into DCR-eligible product [AI]. The Rs 0.7-0.8 crore per MW premium of DCR over non-DCR modules [MC] (CALL Jan 2026) is a premium that exists because of regulation, not because of a cost advantage [AI]. Segment or product margins are not disclosed; management says 'we don't give out any kind of margins by product segment' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

The business is capital-heavy and becoming more so [AI]. Capex was Rs 2,997 crore in FY26, or 38.3% of sales [F] (NUMBERS). CWIP was Rs 2,144 crore at March 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.215), and further capital commitments were Rs 1,034 crore [F] (AR2026 p.275). Management put the 7 GW cell line alone at about Rs 3,000 crore [MC] (CALL May 2026). Inputs are still bought in: 44.10% of procurement was sourced within India [F] (AR2026 p.17), the rest imported. Traded goods (bought-in modules and cells) were Rs 427 crore of FY26 revenue [F] (AR2026 p.262).

blocks.text: Non-DCR modules, Mono PERC cells and EPC are commodity-like [AI]. Management describes non-DCR pricing as set by Chinese supply and passed through [MC] (CALL May 2026). DCR modules and TOPCon cells are differentiated mainly by regulatory eligibility and supply scarcity, not by proprietary technology [AI]. The Kiwa Top Performer recognition [F] (AR2026 p.14) supports bankability but is not a pricing moat [AI].

For FY26 the group reports a single business segment, the solar energy market, and gives geographic information only [F] (AR2026 p.275). From Q1 FY27 the investor presentation shows a two-way split into solar cells and modules, and transformers [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Segment margins are therefore available for one quarter only. Cell versus module margins are not disclosed [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

items: Modules +33%: management attributes this to the ramp-up of new TOPCon module capacity and a higher DCR mix [MC] (RATING, CALL May 2026). Our read is that the gain was mostly volume: module output rose 47% (2,431 MW to 3,570 MW) [F] (AR2026 p.12) while manufactured-module revenue rose 44% [E] (AR2026 p.262), so realisation per MW was flat to slightly down [AI].

Cell output rose 41% [F] (AR2026 p.12), so more cells were consumed internally in DCR modules [AI]. This is consistent with management's aim of shifting away from the 50:50 external/captive split [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
EPC -42%: no management explanation was found. We read it as deliberate de-emphasis while the new HeliosAnthos JV is only starting [AI] (AR2026 p.30).

subsections.title: What is known for FY27 so far

blocks.text: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 2,463 crore, up 35.3% YoY [F] (NUMBERS). Transcon contributed Rs 106.5 crore of operating revenue [F] (PPT Aug 2026), so the solar business grew about 29% organically [E]. Management expects more than two-thirds of the March 2026 order book to be executed in FY27 [MC] (CALL May 2026). By August, 40-45% of the Rs 15,000 crore book was said to fall into FY28 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). First revenue from the 7 GW cell line is targeted for September 2026 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Management gives no revenue guidance for FY27, and we do not create any [AI].

sections.title: Geographic mix, currency and trade policy

blocks.text: Source [F] (AR2026 p.275). No country split and no longer history are disclosed, so a multi-year CAGR cannot be computed. Quarterly exports were 0-1% of revenue through Q1 FY27 [F] (PPT Aug 2026). SCREENER's profile says the company holds 'approximately 100% market share of solar cell exports from India to the United States' [MC] (SCREENER), but with FY26 exports of only Rs 64 crore the claim has little bearing on revenue [AI].

The fall in exports reflects both trade policy and the pull of domestic demand [AI]. In February 2026 the US imposed a preliminary 125.87% countervailing duty on Indian crystalline-silicon cells [F] (AR2026 p.25). Meanwhile domestic DCR margins exceed anything exports can earn [MC] (CALL May 2026). Management's export plans are prospective: a US cell JV with Heliene, output in 24-30 months [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); a European office to open 'shortly' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); and a Singapore subsidiary incorporated on 23 September 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

About 80-85% of the order book is priced in US dollars [MC] (CALL Jan 2026), so revenue moves with USD/INR while imported inputs are also dollar-linked [AI]. Forward cover at March 2026 was USD 182 million plus EUR 1.45 million [F] (AR2026 p.285). A 5% rupee move changes pre-tax profit by Rs 4.3 crore on unhedged balances [F] (AR2026 p.286). FY26 other income included an unrealised FX gain of Rs 32.6 crore [F] (AR2026 p.263).

Utility-scale projects bid before September 2025 are grandfathered and can use imported cells [MC] (CALL May 2026).
ALMM-III for ingots and wafers has been proposed but its final timeline is not confirmed [MC] (CALL Jan 2026, RATING).

All operating plants are in Ranga Reddy district, Telangana, and the new cell and ingot-wafer capacity is at a single Naidupeta site in Andhra Pradesh [F] (AR2026 p.20). The 7 GW cell line is 'in one block' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). That concentrates fire, flood, power and permitting risk [AI].

subsections.title: Contracts: long-term agreements or purchase orders?

blocks.text: Management says cell contracts run into FY28 and FY29 with variable pricing for wafer, silver and FX [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Module orders mostly deliver within 6-9 months [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Frameworks without advances are excluded from the book [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Supporting evidence: customer advances rose from Rs 649 crore to Rs 940 crore in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.263). No contract terms, take-or-pay clauses or cancellation penalties are disclosed.

Read one way, concentration improved [AI]: two customers made up 27% of revenue in FY25 and none exceeded 10% in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.276). Read the other way, it has shifted rather than fallen [AI]. External cell buyers are a small group of domestic module makers blocking capacity [MC] (CALL Nov 2025), and cells are 58% of the order book by value [F] (PPT Aug 2026). A handful of cell offtakers could therefore be large holders of the backlog even though no single customer passes 10% of revenue [AI]. The data cannot tell us which reading is right.

sections.title: Deep dives: DCR cells and modules, transformers, upstream integration

subsections.title: DCR cell-to-module chain (the core of the thesis)

blocks.text: Position in the value chain: Premier converts bought-in wafers into cells and then into ALMM-II-eligible modules [F] (AR2026 p.30). What exists today: 3.6 GW of cells running at 92% effective utilisation in Q1 FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), and 11.1 GW of modules [F] (AR2026 p.6). Management's narrative is 10.6 GW of cells and 'India's largest and most integrated' manufacturer [MC] (CALL Jan 2026); that depends on the 7 GW line, which had only reached trial runs by late August 2026 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Government exposure: demand is heavily programme-linked. PMSGY and KUSUM made up 7.67 GW and 6.72 GW of FY26 distributed additions [F] (AR2026 p.25), and management's FY27 DCR demand estimate of 30 GW+ is built from PMSGY (~10 GW), KUSUM (5-7 GW) and open access [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Both programmes run to March 2027, with successor schemes only 'talked about' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

blocks.text: Position: Transcon makes inverter-duty, power (up to 765 kV), distribution and BESS transformers [F] (AR2026 p.30). What exists: 6.75 GVA operational, a Rs 250 crore order book, and Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 110 crore with PAT of Rs 18 crore [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Narrative: a 10 GVA HV/EHV plant (Neotrafo, a step-down subsidiary) targeted for September 2026 COD [MC] (PPT Aug 2026), with certification taking about six months after commissioning [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Premier's economic share of Neotrafo is about 37% (51% x 72%) [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Premier paid Rs 250 crore for 34.21% [F] (AR2026 p.278), which implies about Rs 731 crore for 100% if the whole payment was for existing shares. That is about 16x FY26 PAT of Rs 45 crore [E]; the split between primary and secondary money is not disclosed. Management's revenue targets have drifted: 'INR1,000 crores plus by FY28' [MC] (CALL Jan 2026) became 'more than triple' about Rs 400 crore 'over the next three years' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The target has slipped by about a year [AI].

blocks.text: Nothing exists yet beyond land, design and building work [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). The planned capex is about Rs 5,900 crore for 10 GW [MC] (CALL Jan 2026), roughly twice the equity raised in the IPO [E] (AR2026 p.202). The investment only pays off if ALMM-III mandates domestic wafers, and management was 'still waiting for the final government announcement' [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Strategically, all three lines point the same way [AI]: returns depend on staying one policy step ahead of new capacity. Each step needs larger, more technology-exposed capex, and the rent from each policy step is time-limited because rivals follow.

subsections.title: Revenue potential from utilisation (sensitivity, not base case)

items: Each additional 1 GW of module output at the FY26 average manufactured-module revenue per MW produced (~Rs 1.62 crore) is worth about Rs 1,620 crore of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.262, p.12).

Each additional 1 GW of external cell sales at ~Rs 1.25 crore per MW (our estimate, assuming half of FY26 cell output was sold externally) is worth about Rs 1,250 crore [E]. Management's quoted cell price is 13.5-14 US cents per watt [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Management's own illustration: 11 GW of modules at 75% utilisation gives about 7-7.5 GW of output [MC] (CALL May 2026), roughly double FY26 output [E]. This is a sensitivity only. Cells consumed in-house do not add revenue twice.

blocks.text: Lease liabilities are small at Rs 90 crore. Undiscounted maturities are Rs 31 crore within one year, Rs 58 crore in years 1-5 and Rs 25 crore beyond five years [F] (AR2026 p.277). They mainly cover office facilities under cancellable arrangements [F] (AR2026 p.276). Land tenure for the plants (owned versus leasehold from state agencies such as APIIC and TSIIC) is not specified in the notes we reviewed. One CARO remark on title deeds at PEGEPL, clause 3(i)(c), suggests at least one property is not held in the company's name [F] (AR2026 p.212).
Capex and ratios [F] (NUMBERS); commitments [F] (AR2026 p.275); Q1 capex [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); Q1 ratios [E].

Sales rose by Rs 4,680 crore between FY24 and FY26, against cumulative FY24-26 capex of Rs 4,066 crore, about Rs 1.15 of revenue per rupee of capex [E] (NUMBERS). On an FY23-FY26 basis the ratio is about 1.6x [E]. The ratio overstates capital efficiency for two reasons [AI]. First, Rs 2,144 crore of CWIP is not yet producing [F] (AR2026 p.215). Second, FY25-26 revenue was lifted by DCR pricing rather than capacity alone. Fixed-asset turnover fell from 6.67x to 4.48x in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: Funding has changed over time. In October 2025 management said the 7 GW expansion was 'funded entirely through internal accruals' and 'we don't plan to take any new debt' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). FY26 then saw Rs 2,214 crore of new long-term borrowings, including a Rs 1,936 crore IREDA loan at 7.95% [F] (AR2026 p.217, p.257). By May 2026 the funding was 'a mix of internal accruals and debt', with a target of debt/equity around 1 and debt/EBITDA of 1.5 or below [MC] (CALL May 2026). In August management said 'bulk of the increase in capacity... has been actually funded by equity' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), and a Rs 5,000 crore enabling resolution followed [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). Classification: capital-heavy [AI].

Key inputs are wafers (for own cells), imported cells (for non-DCR modules), silver paste, glass, aluminium frames, EVA and backsheet [MC] (CALL Jan 2026, CALL May 2026). Only 44.10% of FY26 procurement was sourced in India [F] (AR2026 p.17). Import dependence by country and year is not disclosed. The industry context the company gives is that China holds about 85% of global PV manufacturing capacity and 95% of wafer production [MC] (AR2026 p.23). Indian anodising capacity covers about 20% of frame demand [MC] (CALL Jan 2026).

items: Silver cost per watt rose from about 1 cent to 2.5-2.7 cents over a year [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Silver had 'actually dropped' by August 2026 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
Chinese cell prices rose from 3.5 cents to about 6-6.2 cents per watt, passed through in non-DCR modules [MC] (CALL May 2026).
Glass costs were flat because of minimum import prices; aluminium rose 'slightly' and was offset by frame design changes [MC] (CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: Management's claim: cell contracts are 'variable': wafer, silver and FX pass through [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), and silver risk is passed on in all new orders [MC] (CALL May 2026). The evidence partly supports this [AI]. Quarterly OPM held at 29-31% through the silver spike [F] (NUMBERS). Crisil notes price-variation clauses in 'most' procurement contracts [F] (RATING). But the FY26 hedging reserve shows Rs 30.4 crore of cash-flow-hedge gains recycled to P&L and Rs 6.7 crore capitalised into inventory [F] (AR2026 p.287). Hedging, not only pass-through, cushioned the cost increase [AI]. Our gross-margin proxy fell from 40.1% in Q4 FY26 to 38.5% in Q1 FY27 [E].

subsections.title: Structural versus temporary drivers by year

items: FY24 (OPM 15%): new capacity and early DCR demand; no breakdown is disclosed [AI].

FY25 (OPM 27%): ALMM and DCR demand plus higher cell utilisation (88%) [F] (RATING). A Rs 136 crore warranty charge and a Rs 31.7 crore FX loss depressed EBITDA [F] (AR2026 p.265). Largely structural for the policy period, but policy-dependent [AI].

FY26 (OPM 30%): management credits DCR mix, scale and efficiency [MC] (CALL May 2026). Temporary or judgemental help [F] (AR2026 p.263, p.265): (a) the liquidated-damages line in revenue swung +Rs 156 crore; (b) the warranty charge fell by Rs 75 crore to Rs 61 crore; (c) FX moved from a Rs 31.7 crore loss in expenses to a Rs 32.6 crore gain in other income (outside EBITDA). Items (a) and (b) together are about Rs 231 crore, or 39% of the Rs 597 crore EBITDA increase [E]. Holding both at FY25 levels, FY26 OPM would have been about 28% rather than 30.4% [E].

Q1 FY27 (OPM 29%): Seetharampur costs were booked before revenue, and employee costs rose 72% YoY because of hiring ahead of capacity [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Non-DCR realisations softened [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). PAT margin rose because depreciation fell from Rs 158 crore to Rs 96 crore YoY [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: The move from roughly 5% to roughly 30% OPM is real in cash terms: FY25-26 CFO totalled Rs 2,609 crore [F] (NUMBERS). But it is structural only for as long as DCR scarcity lasts [AI]. Around 2-3 points of the FY26 margin came from items that may not recur [E]. Management's own guide of 29-30% plus or minus 100-150 bp [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) is a stated intention, not a contracted outcome. Crisil treats OPM below 20% as a downgrade trigger [F] (RATING), a sign of how wide the credit analyst's plausible range is [AI].

subsections.title: What can and cannot be built

blocks.text: Production volumes and product revenue are disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.12, p.262). Sales volumes, the captive versus external cell split, the DCR versus non-DCR mix and product-level costs are not disclosed. Management says 'we don't release the actual sales number or the mix between cell and module' [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Any per-unit figures are therefore approximations built on production, not sales. Finished-goods inventory rose by Rs 312 crore in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.264), so FY26 production exceeded sales [AI].

subsections.title: What would have to be true for unit economics to improve

items: The DCR share of module sales has to rise. Management says it will increase 'every quarter' [MC] (CALL May 2026), and our Q1 gross-margin proxy did not show it [E].
The 7 GW line has to reach about 90% usable output within 4-6 months, as the 1.2 GW line did [MC] (CALL Jan 2026), at silver usage 10% lower with 0BB [MC] (CALL May 2026).
DCR prices have to hold at 22-24.5 US cents per watt [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) despite new cell entrants.
Seetharampur's 40% lower manpower per GW [MC] (CALL May 2026) has to show up as falling employee cost per MW, which it did not in Q1 FY27: employee costs rose 72% YoY [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

blocks.text: Our statements data gives seven fiscal years (FY20-FY26), TTM and 12 quarters on a consolidated basis [F] (NUMBERS). Pre-FY24 years reflect a much smaller company and are of limited use for inference [AI]. Quarterly cash flows and balance sheets are not available. The Q1 FY27 figures come from the investor presentation and are unaudited [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

items: Growth is slowing sharply: +107% in FY25, +20% in FY26, and TTM 8.2% above FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Q1 FY27 growth of +35% includes Transcon [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

PAT grew faster than EBITDA because depreciation is volatile. Depreciation was Rs 498 crore in FY25 and Rs 452 crore in FY26, including accelerated charges of Rs 157 crore and Rs 182 crore [F] (AR2026 p.265). It then fell to Rs 70-96 crore per quarter [F] (NUMBERS) and is guided to Rs 240-250 crore per quarter [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

Capitalised borrowing costs rose to Rs 44 crore in FY26 from Rs 12 crore [F] (AR2026 p.264), so reported finance cost of Rs 158 crore understates cash interest [AI]. Cash interest paid was Rs 117 crore [F] (AR2026 p.218).

Other income of Rs 202 crore (AR) includes Rs 42.5 crore of government-grant income, Rs 39 crore of profit on sale of investments and a Rs 32.6 crore unrealised FX gain [F] (AR2026 p.263). It was about 10% of PBT [F] (NUMBERS).
The expected-credit-loss charge was Rs 28 crore in FY26 and the allowance rose to Rs 69 crore [F] (AR2026 p.283), about 7% of gross receivables [E].
Total assets rose 58% to Rs 10,845 crore [F] (AR2026 p.215). CWIP rose from Rs 242 crore to Rs 2,144 crore [F] (NUMBERS).
Borrowings rose from Rs 1,893 crore to Rs 3,617 crore (AR, excluding leases). 84% is floating-rate, and Rs 1,273 crore falls due after five years [F] (AR2026 p.284-285).

Liquid assets: cash Rs 1,467 crore, other bank balances Rs 623 crore and mutual funds Rs 404 crore [F] (AR2026 p.215). Group net debt nevertheless increased. The presentation's net-debt chart peaks at Rs 16,417 million (about Rs 1,642 crore) [F] (PPT Aug 2026), which we read as the June 2026 figure [AI].

Balance with government authorities within other non-current assets jumped from Rs 1 crore to Rs 229 crore [F] (AR2026 p.246). The nature is not explained in the lines we reviewed; it is likely GST/duty credits on capex [AI].
The warranty provision (non-current) rose to Rs 243 crore from Rs 182 crore [F] (AR2026 p.258).

FY26 CFO of Rs 1,261 crore fell despite 61% PAT growth. The working-capital outflow was Rs 775 crore, driven by inventories (-Rs 712 crore) and receivables (-Rs 208 crore), partly offset by payables and customer advances [F] (AR2026 p.217).
FCF was -Rs 1,736 crore in FY26 and cumulative FCF over five years was -Rs 1,782 crore [F] (NUMBERS).
Investing flows include Rs 4,597 crore of mutual-fund purchases and Rs 5,073 crore of redemptions, plus Rs 250 crore for Transcon [F] (AR2026 p.217).
Financing: net borrowing inflow of about Rs 1,723 crore and dividends of Rs 34 crore [F] (AR2026 p.218).

blocks.text: ROE fell from 54.0% to 42.4% and ROCE from 41% to 33% [F] (NUMBERS) as capital built up ahead of output. Debt/equity rose from 0.69 to 0.86 and interest cover improved to 13.5x [F] (NUMBERS). ROCE will fall further in FY27 while Rs 2,144 crore of CWIP and FY27 capex (guided at Rs 5,100 crore [MC] (CALL May 2026)) are commissioned and ramped [AI].

blocks.text: Source [F] (AR2026 p.275). Comfort letters and corporate guarantees mostly back subsidiary borrowings that are already consolidated [AI]. The MOOWR amount becomes payable only if bonded capital goods are cleared for domestic use; management expects no liability [MC] (AR2026 p.275). The balance sheet is sound for today's cash flows and exposed to a margin reset while capex is at its peak [AI].

subsections.title: Auditor, opinion and key audit matters

blocks.text: The auditor is Deloitte Haskins & Sells, appointed at the 26th AGM and proposed for a second five-year term to 2031 [F] (AR2026 p.44, p.305). The FY26 consolidated opinion is unmodified [F] (AR2026 p.207). Key audit matters were revenue cut-off around the balance-sheet date and inventory valuation [F] (AR2026 p.207-208). Both touch the areas of FY26 forensic interest: the finished-goods build and year-end revenue timing [AI]. Three associates, with a Rs 5.1 crore profit share, were audited by other auditors [F] (AR2026 p.210). There is no emphasis of matter [F] (AR2026 p.207-210). The report on internal financial controls is unmodified [F] (AR2026 p.210).

items: CARO remarks in subsidiaries [F] (AR2026 p.212): PEGEPL clause 3(i)(c) (title deeds); Premier Energies Storage Solutions clause 3(vii)(a) (delays in depositing statutory dues); cash-loss remarks under clause 3(xvii) for Zaheerabad, Gajwel, GWC, Storage Solutions, Premier-Green Aluminium and HeliosAnthos.
The audit trail (edit log) operated throughout the year, and the auditors found no tampering [F] (AR2026 p.211).
No revision of financial statements under section 131 [F] (AR2026 p.47). The documents do not report any restatement.
Useful-life re-estimates added Rs 182 crore (FY26) and Rs 157 crore (FY25) of depreciation [F] (AR2026 p.265). This is conservative for those years, but it makes later years look better [AI].
Liquidated damages increased revenue by Rs 76.9 crore in FY26 after reducing it by Rs 79.6 crore in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.263). The cause is not explained.
The warranty charge fell to Rs 61 crore from Rs 136 crore while module revenue rose 33% [F] (AR2026 p.265).
PEIPL is 74% owned, but no profit is attributed to minority holders because the SPA gives the parent the economic interest [F] (AR2026 p.258).
Hedge accounting on silver was adopted in FY26 [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). A net fair-value gain of Rs 6.7 crore on hedging instruments went through OCI [F] (AR2026 p.216).
No common-control transactions were noted in the documents.

subsections.title: Alignment and skin in the game

blocks.text: Promoter holding was 64.25% at September 2024 and 63.94% from September 2025 to March 2026. It fell to 58.48% in June 2026, a drop of 5.46 points in one quarter and 5.77 points over a year [F] (NUMBERS). In the AGM notice the MD alone holds 25.96 crore shares, or 57.31% [F] (AR2026 p.311). subsections.title: Why TAM cannot be translated into company revenue

blocks.text: TAM figures are industry installations, not orders placed with Premier [AI]. As illustrative arithmetic only: FY26 module output of 3,570 MW [F] (AR2026 p.15) against about 60 GW of module demand [MC] (CALL May 2026) is roughly 6% [E]. FY26 cell output of 2,268 MW against 30 GW+ of DCR demand is roughly 8% [E]. Neither share is a target or forecast. Pricing, the non-DCR mix and cell-versus-module choices drive revenue far more than volume share [AI].

Bottom-up framing instead [AI]: revenue is set by (i) usable cell output, up to about 3.3 GW today and up to about 9 GW after the 7 GW ramp by management's 90% rule [MC] (CALL Jan 2026); (ii) the split between external cell sales and captive DCR modules; (iii) DCR module prices of 22-24.5 US cents per watt [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); and (iv) non-DCR modules run only to fill lines. That framing ties revenue to cell capacity and policy rather than to installations.

Module manufacturing is fragmented: 172 GW of capacity against about 60 GW of demand [MC] (AR2026 p.25, CALL May 2026). Cell manufacturing is more concentrated, at 31 GW operational [F] (AR2026 p.25). Management expects 'only about six to eight players' to integrate backwards successfully [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). The channel is split across utility and IPP direct sales, C&I open access, KUSUM tenders run by state agencies, and PMSGY retail through distributors and OEM brands [MC] (CALL May 2026, CALL Jan 2026). Distributed solar is now 'almost 40% of the total market' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

subsections.title: Multiples versus the disclosed peer set

blocks.text: No peer multiples are disclosed in the documents we had, so a peer-relative comparison is not possible [AI]. On its own history, the stock trades at 23.6x trailing earnings at a point where management guides depreciation to rise about 2.5-fold [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The trailing P/E therefore flatters the forward earnings base [AI].

The base DCF gives Rs 470.6 per share, 45.9% below the price [F] (NUMBERS). Main assumptions to challenge [AI]: (i) the 27% margin is below the current 29-30% but above the pre-policy history of 4-15% [F] (NUMBERS); (ii) the 14.4% WACC is high for an A+ rated company but reasonable for a policy-exposed commodity manufacturer; (iii) the 5.5% terminal growth assumes perpetual real growth in a technology-churning industry. Sensible changes to (ii) or (iii) move value by Rs 100-200 per share (grid above), not by the Rs 400 needed [E] (NUMBERS).

At the base margin, WACC and terminal growth, the current EV requires about 36.6% sales growth a year for five years, against a base-case equivalent of 19.8% [F] (NUMBERS). History: 3-year sales CAGR 76.3%, 5-year 62.0%, TTM growth over FY26 8.2% [F] (NUMBERS). The high historical CAGRs come from a Rs 743 crore FY22 base and the start of ALMM [AI]. The current run-rate, with FY26 at +20% and TTM at +8% over FY26, is well below 36.6% [F] (NUMBERS). The bull case starts at 43.5% and fades to 13%, averaging below 36.6% over five years, which is why even the bull value of Rs 729.6 is below the price [E] (NUMBERS).

Key forensic conclusion: the price discounts growth above the bull case, while FY26 EBITDA contained about Rs 231 crore of liquidated-damages and warranty swings [E] (AR2026 p.263, p.265) and forward PAT faces a depreciation step-up of roughly Rs 150 crore per quarter [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

The model applies a flat 27% margin to all revenue and treats the 7 GW line as ordinary growth [AI]. If the line ramps as guided (at least ~70% utilisation in the March 2027 quarter [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)), cell output roughly triples within a year. The cell-to-DCR-module chain could then lift revenue by more than 30% in FY28 at margins the order book supports ('order book has similar margins' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)). Add Transcon and a possible ALMM-III wafer rent, and a period of growth above 36% is not impossible. What is uncertain is whether it lasts five years [AI].

subsections.title: Where the price sits and why

blocks.text: At Rs 870 the shares sit above all three of our DCF values: bear Rs 208.4, base Rs 470.6, bull Rs 729.6 [F] (NUMBERS). The gap comes from the market capitalising FY26-Q1 FY27 margins and growth as long-lived. Our view is that they rest on a policy-created DCR shortage and include several favourable swings [AI]. The operating business is real, well run on existing lines, and backed by contracted volume [AI]. The question for investors is duration and valuation, not whether the business exists [AI].

This is a 12-24 month debate that will be settled mainly by the 7 GW ramp, post-ramp margins and the pace of domestic cell-capacity additions [AI]. Re-review at: (1) Q2 FY27 results (Nov 2026), for first 7 GW revenue, the depreciation step and the half-year balance sheet with inventory and advances; (2) Q3 FY27 results (Jan-Feb 2027), for the end of the ALMM-II exemption and the order book; (3) Q4 FY27 results and the FY27 annual report, for the warranty charge, liquidated damages, customer concentration and capex versus plan [AI]. Also re-review immediately on any QIP launch, further promoter selling, or ALMM-III / BCD notifications [AI].

This is our initial coverage of Premier Energies; there is no previous report to compare against. We have instead tested earlier management guidance from the November 2025, January 2026 and May 2026 calls against outcomes in the guidance tracker [AI].

summary.one_line: Premier Energies is running a genuinely strong integrated cell-and-module business that is benefiting from India's domestic-content rules, but at Rs 870 the shares sit above even the bull-case DCF value of Rs 729.6: the price needs about 37% annual sales growth for five years. Meanwhile FY26 margins were helped by one-off swings and depreciation is guided to rise about 2.5-fold.
bull_points: Contracted visibility: the order book is about Rs 15,000 crore (9,867 MW) at 30 June 2026, about 1.8x FY26 revenue, supported by Rs 940 crore of customer advances [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [F] (RATING); [F] (AR2026 p.262).

Margin resilience: operating EBITDA margin held at 29-31% for five straight quarters through the silver and commodity spike [F] (NUMBERS), and management guides 29-30% plus or minus 100-150 bp [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

Capacity step-change: the 7 GW TOPCon cell line takes cell capacity from 3.6 GW to 10.6 GW, with first revenue targeted for September 2026 and at least ~70% utilisation in the March 2027 quarter [F] (AR2026 p.6); [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
Credit strength: Crisil upgraded the rating to A+/Positive on 17 August 2026, with net debt/EBITDA about 0.4x and interest cover of about 16x at FY26 [F] (RATING).

Diversification optionality: Transcon posted Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 110 crore at a 24.3% operating EBITDA margin, with a 10 GVA EHV plant targeted for September 2026 [F] (PPT Aug 2026); [MC] (PPT Aug 2026).
bear_points: Valuation: the price of Rs 870 exceeds all three DCF values (bear Rs 208.4, base Rs 470.6, bull Rs 729.6), and the reverse DCF implies 36.6% sales CAGR against 19.8% in the base case [E] (NUMBERS).

The margin depends on policy: management says non-DCR business 'is not profitable as we speak' with ~250 GW of module lines against ~60 GW of demand, and ALMM-II has already been temporarily relaxed for C&I to December 2026 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [F] (PPT Aug 2026).

Earnings quality: about Rs 231 crore of FY26 EBITDA came from a liquidated-damages revenue swing and a lower warranty charge, and FY26 CFO/PAT fell to 0.84 as finished goods doubled [E] (AR2026 p.263, p.265); [F] (NUMBERS).
Depreciation step-up: quarterly depreciation of Rs 96 crore in Q1 FY27 is guided to Rs 240-250 crore in Q3-Q4 FY27, a post-tax drag of roughly Rs 110-117 crore per quarter [MC] (CALL Aug 2026); [E].

Capital intensity and credibility: FY26 FCF was -Rs 1,736 crore, borrowings nearly doubled despite a 'no new debt' statement, a Rs 5,000 crore capital-raise enabling resolution was passed, and project dates (4.8 GW cells, BESS, Transcon capacity, KSolare) slipped [F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL Nov 2025); [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS).
